data.completion_memo: Send is no longer disabled by workflow/model readiness, and every remaining disable is explained on screen. `composer.ts::canSubmit` dropped the `workflowReadinessError`/`workflowChecking` conditions and the `ComposerReadiness` parameter entirely (workflow/model readiness is not a disable condition); the empty-draft reason is now the exported `emptyDraftReason` so the UI can treat it as self-evident. `ChatComposer.tsx` renders any other `disabledReason` as a visible `role="status"` line with an `aria-describedby` link from the button, and renders a `role="alert"` warning notice when `workflowReadinessError` is set while keeping Send enabled and its title carrying the rule+remedy; the core still refuses a start with the same reason, which already reaches the status bar. `ChatWorkspaceScreen.tsx` no longer tracks/forwards `workflowChecking` (the removed gate); the readiness effect only updates the notice. Added `.composer-notices`/`.composer-notice`/`-warning` styles. Tests: `chat.test.ts` updated (readiness is no longer a canSubmit concern) and a new `composerSubmission.test.tsx` case proves Send stays enabled and the rule+remedy is announced for a non-executable workflow verdict. Verified: `pnpm check` (tsc) clean and the whole `pnpm test:chat` suite (44 files, 287 tests) passes.

lines:
Symptom: with a workflow whose model is not configured, the Chat submit button is disabled and the user is never told why. The user does not accept a silently disabled Send button.
Root cause (researched): `canSubmit` (`desktop/src/chat/composer.ts:34-61`) returns `workflowReadinessError` (line 52-56) and `workflowChecking` (57-58); `ChatComposer.tsx:199-208` turns the return value into `disabledReason` and renders it **only** as the disabled button's `title` (437-455). The readiness data is computed in `ChatWorkspaceScreen.tsx:498-553` from `workflow_snapshot`'s `executionVerdict.rule/remedy` (service.rs:626-703) but has no visible surface. A refused start would already produce a visible error notice via `useChatRuntime`/`useChatErrorNotices`, but the disabled button prevents it.
Fix: (1) stop disabling Send for workflow readiness/checking — the button must be enabled whenever a message can be attempted; a bad workflow is reported by the core refusal and must not be a dead end. (2) Always render the remaining disabled reasons visibly next to the control (not only as a tooltip), with `aria-describedby`. (3) Surface workflow/model readiness as a clear in-UI warning (inline composer notice and/or status-bar condition notice) carrying the rule+remedy, so the user knows exactly what to fix. Keep genuinely inapplicable states (empty draft, terminal Chat, recovery pending, awaiting answer) failing safely, but explained.
Verification: update/extend `chat.test.ts` (canSubmit) and `composerSubmission.test.tsx` to assert the readiness condition no longer disables Send and that a visible reason is rendered.

data.title: Never disable the Chat submit button without a visible reason; surface workflow/model readiness
